transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Well, I guess what brings me in is this constant restless feeling I have. It's like I’m just wound way too tight all the time and I can’t fully settle. Even when I’m supposed to be calmly sitting through a planning meeting at work... I'm a retail buyer, and right now we're looking at the spring apparel lines, which honestly is a total headache this year because the shipping delays from our overseas vendors are just completely out of hand. I was dealing with a supplier in Milan all week and they keep messing up the invoices, and the fabrics aren't even what we agreed on. 

But anyway, even when I'm away from all that and trying to relax, like when I'm painting or doing yoga, I still feel that restless way. I'll be in yoga class and the instructor will be telling us to breathe and find our center, and I just can't settle down. I just end up sitting there on the mat thinking about whether I should have ordered more of the floral blouses instead of the geometric ones for the April catalog...
About how long have you been feeling this restless and wound up?

Well, it’s been noticeably harder to manage for... I'd say about two years and two months? That’s really when the in-law conflicts started taking over more of our evenings. My husband's mother, she just has this habit of coming over right when we're trying to wind down, and she always brings her little Pomeranian. Which, don't get me wrong, I like dogs, but it sheds everywhere. 

I had just bought this beautiful cream-colored rug for the living room—it’s a Moroccan trellis pattern, absolutely gorgeous, I actually got a fantastic deal on it through some wholesale home goods connections at work—and she just lets the dog run all over it with dirty paws. And then she starts making these little passive-aggressive comments about how I'm maintaining the house, and my husband just sits there watching the news! It’s just so frustrating. I mean, I spend my whole day negotiating with international vendors and dealing with shipping manifests, I don't want to come home and negotiate boundaries in my own living room while picking dog hair off a wool rug... 

Wait, I'm sorry, what did you ask me? Oh, right, the timeline. But yes, about two years and a couple of months since it got really hard to manage.
Do you find it difficult to control or stop these worries once they start?

Well, it's not so much that I worry, it's more just... I can't stop moving or doing things. Like I said, I'm just wound tight. I don't really sit around and fret about things, I just feel like I need to be up and doing something. Which is why it's so annoying when my mother-in-law comes over, because I'll be right in the middle of trying to organize the pantry or something—I just got these amazing clear acrylic bins, they were on clearance at a home goods show I went to in Chicago last month. The show was actually really disappointing overall, the vendors didn't have anything fresh, just the same old farmhouse chic stuff that's been out for five years. But the bins were a great find. 

Anyway, I'll be trying to organize, and she'll come in and just expect me to sit down and have tea and chat, and I just can't. I literally can't just sit there on the sofa while there are things to do. I end up pacing around the kitchen island while she talks. So, no, it's not really worries that I can't stop. It's just the physical feeling of needing to go, go, go.
Over these past two years, have you also had periods where you felt down, depressed, or had very low energy?

No, I wouldn't say I feel down or depressed. I definitely don't have low energy, that's for sure! I mean, I'm always on the move. Even when I'm exhausted, my body just wants to keep going. It's like I have this motor inside me that just won't shut off. 

Speaking of motors, my husband just bought this vintage sports car—an old MG from the 70s. He's been spending every weekend in the garage tinkering with it. He says it's his "midlife crisis" project, but honestly, it just smells like oil and old leather in there. And he tracked grease onto the driveway, which I had just power-washed. I spent an entire Saturday morning out there with the pressure washer, which, by the way, is incredibly satisfying. Have you ever used one? Watching the dirt just blast away from the concrete... it's amazing. I actually thought about starting a little side business doing power washing because it's so fun, but then I remembered I already have a full-time job dealing with those overseas shipping manifests, which are a nightmare right now. 

But anyway, no, I don't really get depressed or low energy. I just have too much energy, if anything.
Looking back to when you were a child before age 12, were you also very restless, constantly on the go, or having trouble sitting still?

Oh, definitely. I remember back in elementary school, my parents were always getting notes sent home from my teachers because I just kept popping out of my seat during lessons. I was always talking over my classmates, too, and I'd just rush to blurt out the answers before the teacher even finished asking the question. I just couldn't wait! 

Speaking of notes, my mother actually kept all of those old school reports in this massive scrapbook. She is absolutely obsessed with scrapbooking. She goes to these huge craft conventions—actually, I went with her to one in Orlando a few years ago because I was scouting some boutique paper vendors for a potential retail line at work. The markup on specialty cardstock is unbelievable, by the way. You wouldn't believe what people will pay for some embossed vellum and a bit of gold foil. We ended up not going with that supplier, though, because their shipping terms were completely ridiculous and inflexible. I mean, if you can't guarantee a net-30 payment structure and reliable freight, I can't work with you. 

But anyway... yes, I was definitely like this back then too. Always jumping out of my chair and talking out of turn.
